evidence.approach: Identity by content, as clarify decided (record 6, measured at notes 2 and 5). One new function in harness/calibration.py, `finding_identities(records)`, returns a map from (record sequence, position) to an identity: every review finding read through `_review_findings` is joined to every other that names the same normalised file (via `path_of`) and carries the same `claim` or the same `failure_scenario`, transitively, with a small union-find; a finding with neither text is an identity of its own. The id is never read. `latest_finding_records` groups by that identity, most recent record winning, exactly as it does by key today; `escapes` replaces its per-finding `finding_key` call with a lookup in the same map, so it still takes the earliest round of each identity. `finding_key` is deleted: its only caller is `escapes` (codegraph impact, record 4, and grep), and a pairwise key cannot express a transitive join, which is what SEEN-107's G1 needs (its claim changed between rounds while its failure_scenario did not). `kpi.findings` changes no code, only its docstring, which says what the count now rests on and names SEEN-006's residue. The weekly report for the week SEEN-107 delivered (2026-W39) and the sprint 0 report are regenerated with `harness report`; both are derived from the journals by cli.ticket_figures, so the corrected figure reaches them without touching report.py.
changes: harness/calibration.py: add `finding_identities(records)`; `latest_finding_records` groups by it; `escapes` looks identities up in it instead of calling `finding_key`; delete `finding_key`. Docstrings say why the id is not read and cite SEEN-107 and SEEN-102.

harness/kpi.py: the `findings` docstring states what a finding's identity rests on (same file, and the same claim or the same failure scenario, never the id) and the residue it does not catch (a finding reworded in every field, SEEN-006's R-04).
harness/tests/test_calibration.py: a `FindingIdentityTest` class with the fixture tests and the tests over the committed journals.
docs/harness/reports/2026-W39.md, 2026-W39.json, sprint-0.md, sprint-0.json: regenerated by `python3 harness/run.py report --week --date 2026-09-24` and `--sprint 0`.
docs/tickets/SEEN-145-count-a-review-finding-once-however-the.md: Outcome, status and ticks at review, as the procedure requires.
tests_first: Two review advances whose findings differ only in their ids count once. `python3 -m unittest harness.tests.test_calibration.FindingIdentityTest -v`. RED: kpi.findings over a fixture of two review advances, the first carrying F1 and the second R1-1 with the same claim, failure_scenario, file and severity, returns by_severity summing to 2 where the test asserts 1.

A finding whose claim was reworded but whose failure_scenario was carried is one finding. Same command. RED: two advances, same file and scenario, claims differing, ids differing; latest_findings returns 2 where the test asserts 1. This is the G1/R2-1 shape from SEEN-107.
SEEN-107's committed journal reports 26. Same command. RED: kpi.findings over journal.read(docs/harness/history/SEEN-107) sums to 45 where the test asserts 26.

Every committed journal reports its pinned figure. Same command. RED: a table of all 29 journals present at clarify, every one at today's figure except SEEN-107 at 26 and SEEN-102 at 4, fails on exactly those two; the same test pins each journal's escapes and unattributable counts at today's values, which pass before and after.

Guards that pass before and after and must stay green: two findings sharing an id but differing in claim, scenario and file are two (the id collision across rounds in SEEN-109 and SEEN-113); a finding with no claim and no scenario is not merged with another such finding; and the existing SecondReviewTest cases (carried-forward finding is one, charged to the earliest round).

slices.name: Finding identity by content, pinned on every journal, reports regenerated
slices.red: FindingIdentityTest fails before calibration.py changes: the different-ids fixture counts 2 against 1, the reworded-claim fixture counts 2 against 1, SEEN-107's journal counts 45 against 26, and the all-journals table fails on SEEN-107 and SEEN-102 only.

alternatives: Count only the review advance that was accepted (the ticket's first shape). Rejected on the journals, note 2: SEEN-008, SEEN-106 and SEEN-114 end on an advance carrying no findings while their returns carry 86, 20 and 34, and SEEN-088's three advances are disjoint.

Key on (claim, file) alone, a drop-in change to finding_key. Rejected: SEEN-107 comes out at 27, because G1 was reworded while its failure_scenario was carried, and a pairwise key cannot join on either of two fields.
Keep the id as a tiebreak so SEEN-102 stays at 7. Rejected at clarify on Ruud's decision (criterion 3 amended): it is the dependence the ticket removes.

Fuzzy matching on the claim (a similarity ratio) to catch SEEN-006's R-04. Rejected at clarify: a threshold is a judgement a session could tune, and the ticket's point is a figure that does not rest on what a session writes.
Rewrite the delivered kpi.json of SEEN-107 and SEEN-102. Rejected at clarify (note 5): the receipt does not hash them, they record what delivery computed, and the reports derive from journals.
risks: A transitive join over-merges: two genuinely different findings in one file that happen to share a boilerplate failure_scenario become one. Mitigated by the all-journals table, which shows no journal but the two intended ones moves, and by a guard test that two findings sharing only an id are two. Residual: a future review reusing a scenario word for word for a different finding would be undercounted; the kpi docstring says so.

The tests over committed journals break when a pinned journal gains records. The journals pinned are delivered and append-only; a reopen of one of them would legitimately change its figure and the test names the ticket, so the failure says where to look. Journals created after this ticket are not pinned, and the test says so rather than iterating whatever is present.

Regenerating the sprint and weekly reports carries every change since they were last written on 24 September, not only this ticket's. Mitigated by reading the regenerated diff and recording in the tdd record which rows moved and why; the claim this ticket makes of them is SEEN-107 at 26 and SEEN-102 at 4 only.

Report figures that read session logs (tokens, tool calls) depend on this machine's logs. The regenerated reports are checked for those columns changing for tickets whose findings did not; if they do, that is recorded rather than committed silently.
evidence.rollback: Revert the merge commit. The change touches no record format, no gate and no stored data; the reports are derived and are regenerated by the same command after the revert.
